authors: Nathalie Hubert, Mohammed Bouroukba, Louis Schuffenecker
title: Aqueous solution of sodium sulfate. Determination of the dissolution enthalpy at 25, 27.5 and 45 C
experimental_method: Setaram C80D differential calorimeter, mixing cell with known mass of solid Na2SO4 and twice distilled water by inverting mechanism, reference cell with water of equal total mass; calibrated with indium fusion and NaCl dissolution at 25 C.
uncertainties_stated: Precision of the results about 2%. Lowest molality (0.28) set by calorimeter sensitivity.
quality_remarks: Text layer is OCR-quality; digits verified against page images. Nominal temperatures in text 24.4, 27.5, 44.3 C; no temperature scale, no pressure stated. Table 4 gives fitted Pitzer parameters, not data. Saturation limits derived from plateau (3.64 and 3.57 mol/kg). Table 4 of the paper lists 300.35 K (27.2 C) for the 27.5 C series, whereas text, Table 2 title and Fig. 3 say 27.5 C: a paper inconsistency, the 27.5 C constant is kept. The tabulated quantity is the integral enthalpy of dissolution of the solid salt at the stated final molality.
how_extracted: pdf_text_layer, checked cell by cell against 170 dpi page images
not_extracted_tables: Table 4 (Pitzer-model fit parameters and fitted infinite-dilution dissolution enthalpies): fitted/model parameters, not measured values
changes_after_image_check: Table 3 row 4 dHexp and dH^: text layer '--12.48', '--8320' -> -12.48, -8320 (double dash artefact)

extraction_notes: Value mapping: value = dHexp/n1 (J per mol Na2SO4, authors' calculation Eq. 7), value2 = raw dHexp (J), value3 = dH^ per kg water. Sanity: n1/k = n1/(nw*0.0180153) spot-checked by script; enthalpy decreases to plateau as stated. Columns of Table 1: replicate nw values (0.2942, 0.0555 etc) are different n1.
